claims.claim_text: initializeBattle transitions status to 'playing', turn to 'player', resets both health pools (enemy pool from options.enemyMaxHealth, default 100), seeds battleLog with 'A wild monster appears!' (type 'system'), resets streak/xpEarned/poses/inputLocked/revealedTranslation.

claims.claim_text: damagePlayer clamps playerHealth at 0 and, only when status is 'playing' and resulting health is <= 0, transitions status to 'defeat' and playerPose to 'defeat'; otherwise playerPose becomes 'hurt'.
claims.interpretation: playing -> defeat is guarded by the health floor; non-lethal damage still emits a hurt pose.

claims.claim_text: damageEnemy clamps enemyHealth at 0 and, only when status is 'playing' and resulting health is <= 0, transitions status to 'victory', enemyPose to 'defeat', and playerPose to 'victory'; otherwise enemyPose becomes 'hurt'.
claims.interpretation: playing -> victory is guarded by the enemy health floor and sets both terminal poses.

claims.claim_text: enemyAttack is a no-op unless status === 'playing' and turn === 'enemy'; when valid it sets enemyPose to 'basic-attack', turn back to 'player', then applies damagePlayer(damage) with default damage 8.
claims.interpretation: The enemy-turn -> player-turn transition is bundled with the counterattack damage and pose change, and is guarded against out-of-turn invocation.

claims.claim_text: submitAnswer on a correct (case-insensitive, trimmed) match: inputLocked=false, revealedTranslation=null, streak+1, playerPose 'power-attack' when attackPower is 'power' else 'basic-attack'; returns true.
claims.interpretation: Correct answer drives the streak increment and attack pose transition.

claims.claim_text: submitAnswer on an incorrect match: inputLocked=true, revealedTranslation=expected, streak reset to 0, playerPose 'miss'; a 2000ms timeout then clears inputLocked and revealedTranslation; returns false.
claims.interpretation: Incorrect answer imposes a 2-second input lockout with the correct translation revealed, and breaks the streak.

claims.claim_text: selectHero transitions selectionStep 'hero' -> 'location' and records selectedHeroId; it is a no-op unless the current step is 'hero'.
claims.interpretation: Wizard step 1->2 is order-enforced.

claims.claim_text: selectLocation transitions selectionStep 'location' -> 'enemy' and records selectedLocationId; no-op unless current step is 'location'.
claims.interpretation: Wizard step 2->3 is order-enforced.

claims.claim_text: selectEnemy transitions selectionStep 'enemy' -> 'ready' and records selectedEnemyId; no-op unless current step is 'enemy'.
claims.interpretation: Wizard step 3->4 (terminal) is order-enforced; 'ready' closes the modal.

claims.claim_text: resetSelection returns selectionStep to 'hero' and clears all three selected ids.
claims.interpretation: Selection wizard is fully restartable; the page calls it whenever vocabulary reloads outside the start screen.

claims.claim_text: A page effect transitions the game from selection to battle: when selectionStep === 'ready' with hero and enemy chosen, it resolves sprites and calls initializeBattle({ enemyMaxHealth: scaleEnemyHealth(enemy.multiplier) }).
claims.interpretation: Reaching selectionStep 'ready' is the trigger that actually starts the battle (status idle -> playing) with enemy-scaled health.

claims.claim_text: triggerEnemyTurn (page.tsx) rolls enemy damage via rollEnemyDamage(enemyMultiplier), sets turn to 'enemy', then after 600ms applies enemyAttack(damage), spawns '-{damage}' floating text at the player position, increments turnsTaken, sets flashTone 'player', bumps flashKey and shakeKey, logs 'Enemy strikes back!' (type 'enemy'), and plays 'missile-hit'.
claims.interpretation: The player-turn -> enemy-turn transition is animated with a fixed 600ms delay and full audiovisual feedback.

claims.claim_text: handleSubmit early-returns unless status === 'playing', inputLocked is false, and turn === 'player'.
claims.interpretation: Player input is accepted only on the player's turn during active play with no lockout.

claims.claim_text: On a matched answer, handleSubmit computes damage, calls submitAnswer, plays 'success', speaks the term via speechSynthesis, updates performance, logs 'You cast {term}!', applies damageEnemy, spawns enemy damage text, has a ~20% chance to schedule a 'CRITICAL!' text, increments turnsTaken, sets flashTone 'enemy', clears the input, and triggers the enemy turn only if the enemy survives.
claims.interpretation: A correct answer is a full player-turn resolution pipeline ending in either the enemy counterattack or (on lethal damage) the victory transition from damageEnemy.

claims.claim_text: On an unmatched answer, handleSubmit submits against the fallback action (the 'power' action or the first), plays 'error', records a miss in performance, logs 'Incorrect! The spell was {translation}.', clears the input, and triggers the enemy turn.
claims.interpretation: An incorrect answer always costs the player a turn: the enemy counterattacks after the reveal pipeline.

claims.claim_text: A page effect watches status: when status becomes 'victory' or 'defeat' it computes accuracy, computes base XP via calculateRpgBattleXp, scales it by the enemy multiplier, persists via handleGameComplete, and reveals the results screen after a 1200ms timeout; any non-terminal status hides results.
claims.interpretation: Terminal-status -> results-surface transition is delayed 1.2s and includes XP computation and a completion POST.

claims.claim_text: handleRestart resets all page-local states (input, turns, streak, flash/shake keys, flashTone 'enemy', results, XP, accuracy, performance), sets showStartScreen true and status 'idle', increments gameKey, and exits fullscreen.
claims.interpretation: Restart returns the game to the start-screen + idle status and re-enters the selection wizard (via the vocabulary effect calling resetSelection).

claims.claim_text: handleStartBattle sets showStartScreen false and enters fullscreen.
claims.interpretation: Start-screen -> selection-modal transition (the selection modal renders whenever showStartScreen is false and step is not 'ready').

claims.claim_text: A page effect calls resetSelection() and setStatus('idle') whenever vocabulary is loaded and the start screen is not showing.
claims.interpretation: Vocabulary reload forces the selection wizard back to step 'hero' and status 'idle'.

claims.claim_text: The T2 denominator records three unresolved transition write candidates for flashTone in the advantage-games page.tsx: line 354 -> 'player', line 403 -> 'enemy', line 434 -> 'enemy', each with reason 'no-single-proven-from-state'.
claims.interpretation: flashTone writes at 354 (enemy counterattack), 403 (player hit), and 434 (restart) are collector-confirmed; the denominator deliberately left their from-states unproven, and this ledger records the to-states with exact lines without inferring provenance beyond the code.

claims.claim_text: The same three flashTone write candidates exist in the reading-advantage page.tsx at lines 343 (-> 'player'), 392 (-> 'enemy'), and 423 (-> 'enemy') per the T2 denominator; the 11-line offset matches the RA page being 17 lines shorter overall.
claims.interpretation: flashTone write sites are structurally mirrored in the RA copy at shifted line numbers.

claims.claim_text: The T2 scene-state denominator contains zero proven transitions for RPG Battle (transitions: 0) and exactly six unresolved transition write candidates (3 per host page).
claims.interpretation: The mechanical pipeline could not prove any single from-state for RPG Battle transitions; all transition claims in this ledger (RPG-TR-001..019) are collector-collected from source with exact lines, which is the pilot's purpose.

claims.claim_text: Page constants: ACTION_COUNT = 3, BASIC_DAMAGE = 10, POWER_DAMAGE = 18, MAX_TURNS = 12 (page.tsx lines 49-52).
claims.interpretation: Three vocabulary actions are offered per battle; correct answers deal 10 (basic) or 18 (power) base damage.

claims.claim_text: MAX_TURNS is referenced exactly twice in non-test source: its declaration (line 52) and as the maxTurns argument to calculateRpgBattleXp (line 289). No code enforces a turn limit that ends the battle.
claims.interpretation: The 12-turn figure is an XP-efficiency denominator only; a battle can last arbitrarily many turns. grep of apps/advantage-games/src for MAX_TURNS confirms only these two hits.

claims.claim_text: Correct-answer damage = (power === 'power' ? POWER_DAMAGE : BASIC_DAMAGE) + Math.floor(streak / 2).
claims.interpretation: Streak adds +1 damage per 2 consecutive correct answers on top of the tiered base damage.

claims.claim_text: Post-damage enemy health is computed as Math.max(0, enemyHealth - damage) and the enemy counterattack fires only when that value is > 0.
claims.interpretation: Lethal player hits suppress the enemy counterattack.

claims.claim_text: scaleEnemyHealth(multiplier, baseHealth = BASE_ENEMY_HEALTH = 100) returns Math.round(baseHealth * multiplier).
claims.interpretation: Enemy HP scales linearly with the selection multiplier from a base of 100.

claims.claim_text: Enemy damage rolls use BASE_ENEMY_DAMAGE_MIN = 6 and BASE_ENEMY_DAMAGE_MAX = 10: getEnemyDamageRange returns { min: 6, max: max(6, round(10 * multiplier)) } and rollEnemyDamage returns a uniform integer in that inclusive range.
claims.interpretation: Enemy damage floor is always 6; only the ceiling scales with the multiplier (elemental 2x -> 6..20, spectre 1.5x -> 6..15, goblin 1x -> 6..10, slime 0.5x -> 6..6).

claims.claim_text: battleEnemies defines four enemies with multipliers: slime 0.5, goblin 1, spectre 1.5, elemental 2 (rpgBattleSelection.ts lines 62-87).
claims.interpretation: Enemy choice is the difficulty knob, scaling both enemy HP and XP and the enemy damage ceiling.

claims.claim_text: battleHeroes defines two cosmetic heroes ('male', 'female') with 3x3 pose-sheet sprites, and battleLocations defines four backgrounds (forest-clearing, ruined-road, magic-arena, throne-hall).
claims.interpretation: Hero and location selections carry no stats; only the enemy has a multiplier. BattleSelectionModal copy confirms: 'Cosmetic choice only.' / 'Background only.'

claims.claim_text: calculateRpgBattleXp computes healthRatio (weight 0.6) + turnEfficiency (weight 0.4) + streakBoost (up to 0.2), maps the clamped score to round(1 + score * 9), and clamps the result to 1..10 XP.
claims.interpretation: Base XP is always between 1 and 10, rewarding high remaining health, few turns, and long streaks.

claims.claim_text: Final XP = scaleBattleXp(baseXp, enemyMultiplier) = Math.round(baseXp * multiplier) (page.tsx lines 292-293; rpgBattleScaling.ts lines 16-18).
claims.interpretation: The enemy multiplier scales end-of-battle XP (elemental doubles it; slime halves it).

claims.claim_text: selectBattleActions weights each vocabulary word by MIN_WEIGHT (0.25) + difficulty, where difficulty = clamp(1 - accuracy, 0, 1); words with difficulty >= POWER_THRESHOLD (0.5) become 'power' actions; selection is weighted-random without replacement up to count (default 3).
claims.interpretation: Harder (less-accurate) words are more likely to be offered and hit harder; unseen words have accuracy 0 -> difficulty 1 -> always 'power'.

claims.claim_text: The fallback for an unmatched typed answer is the action with power 'power', or actions[0] if none (page.tsx lines 369-370); the miss is recorded against that fallback term (line 417).
claims.interpretation: A wrong guess damages the player's performance stats on the hardest offered word.

claims.claim_text: Answer matching is exact after trim + lowercase normalization of both the input and the expected translation (store submitAnswer lines 134-136; page handleSubmit lines 365-368).
claims.interpretation: No fuzzy/partial matching; case and surrounding whitespace are ignored.

claims.claim_text: Accuracy at battle end = totalCorrect / totalAttempts across the per-word performance map, or 0 when there were no attempts (page.tsx lines 223-231, 283).
claims.interpretation: Accuracy aggregates every submitted answer in the battle.

claims.claim_text: turnsTaken is clamped to a minimum of 1 when sent to the completion API (line 247) and to the XP formula (line 288).
claims.interpretation: A zero-turn battle (impossible in normal flow) cannot divide XP efficiency by zero.

claims.claim_text: longestStreak tracks the maximum streak seen (page effect lines 214-216) and feeds the XP streakBoost; the live streak resets to 0 on any incorrect answer (store line 156).
claims.interpretation: The XP formula rewards the best streak of the battle, not the final streak.

claims.claim_text: ComboIndicator renders a 'COMBO x{streak}' badge only when streak >= 2 (ComboIndicator.tsx line 10).
claims.interpretation: The combo UI is purely cosmetic feedback for consecutive correct answers.

claims.claim_text: A 'CRITICAL!' floating text is scheduled with probability Math.random() > 0.8 (~20%) 200ms after a correct hit (page.tsx lines 397-401); it does not alter damage.
claims.interpretation: Critical hits are cosmetic only - the damage number is computed before and independently of the crit text.

claims.claim_text: On a correct answer the matched term is spoken via window.speechSynthesis with lang 'en-US' and rate 1.0, guarded by a browser-capability check (page.tsx lines 386-391).
claims.interpretation: The game includes TTS of the English term as a learning reinforcement.

claims.claim_text: There is no mana/MP system: grep -rni 'mana' over the rpg-battle components, page, store, and rpgBattle libs returns no non-test match at the baseline.
claims.interpretation: Player actions are gated by turn order and input lockout, not by any resource pool. Negative claim verified by full-text search (command recorded in the evidence method document).

claims.claim_text: There is no defend/guard action available to the player: the 'defend' pose exists in the pose vocabulary but no producer sets playerPose or enemyPose to 'defend' anywhere outside tests (grep-verified).
claims.interpretation: The defend pose is a dead state at the baseline - reserved by the asset spec but unimplemented.
claims.verification_command: grep -rn "'defend'" apps/advantage-games/src --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' (only type unions and tests match)

claims.claim_text: The completion POST body contains xp, accuracy, totalAttempts, totalCorrect, turnsTaken (min 1), heroId, enemyId, and outcome ('victory'|'defeat') (page.tsx lines 233-252).
claims.interpretation: Client-reported XP is sent to the host API; in advantage-games the mock route recomputes XP server-side via calculateGameXP instead of trusting the body.

claims.claim_text: The advantage-games mock complete route validates the body with gameCompletionInputSchema, computes xpEarned via calculateGameXP, and returns { xpEarned, activityId: 'game:<gameType>:<idempotencyKey>', duplicate: false, status: 200 }; it deliberately does not persist (no DB/auth/tenant).
claims.interpretation: The standalone app demonstrates the completion contract without persistence.

claims.claim_text: The advantage-games vocabulary route returns the static SAMPLE_VOCABULARY list with warning 'NO_VOCABULARY' when empty and 'INSUFFICIENT_VOCABULARY' with requiredCount 5 when fewer than 5 words exist.
claims.interpretation: The 5-word minimum enforced by the page (line 163) mirrors the route contract.

claims.claim_text: SAMPLE_VOCABULARY contains 25 Thai->English term/translation pairs (e.g. 'สวัสดี'->'Hello') used by the advantage-games vocabulary route.
claims.interpretation: The standalone app ships Thai source terms with English translations, matching the typed-translation mechanic.

claims.claim_text: The page requires data.vocabulary.length >= 5 before accepting the fetched vocabulary, otherwise it shows the notEnoughWords error (page.tsx lines 163-167).
claims.interpretation: A battle cannot start with fewer than 5 words.

claims.claim_text: menuActions maps the 3 selected BattleActions to { id, label: term, power } for the ActionMenu display (page.tsx lines 324-332).
claims.interpretation: The action menu shows the English term as a label and its power tier; the player must type the translation.

claims.claim_text: The primary battle input is a text input ('Type translation...', aria-label 'Action input') inside a form; submitting the form (Enter key or Cast button) calls onSubmit with the trimmed value, blocked when disabled or empty (ActionMenu.tsx lines 40-48, 76-94).
claims.interpretation: RPG Battle is a typing game: keyboard text entry plus form submission is the core control.

claims.claim_text: The ActionMenu input is disabled and the Cast button disabled unless there is non-whitespace input; the page passes disabled = inputLocked || turn !== 'player' || status !== 'playing' (page.tsx lines 595-597).
claims.interpretation: Controls lock out during the enemy turn, during the 2s answer reveal, and outside active play.

claims.claim_text: The input auto-focuses whenever the menu becomes enabled (useEffect on disabled, lines 34-38) and via autoFocus={!disabled} (line 83).
claims.interpretation: Keyboard focus is managed so the player can type immediately when their turn begins.

claims.claim_text: Selection wizard choices are pointer/click buttons: SelectionOptionButton renders a Button with onClick={onSelect} for each hero, location, and enemy option (BattleSelectionModal.tsx lines 42-66, 117-176).
claims.interpretation: Pre-battle selection is click/tap driven.

claims.claim_text: StartScreen tab switching is click-driven (onClick={() => setActiveTab(tab.id)}, lines 109-124); the rankings enemy selector is also click-driven (lines 231-262); the Start Battle button fires onStart (lines 371-380).
claims.interpretation: All start-screen navigation is pointer-based.

claims.claim_text: No keyboard event handlers (keydown/keyup/addEventListener) exist anywhere in the rpg-battle components, page, store, or libs at the baseline (grep-verified, exit 1).
claims.interpretation: Beyond native form/input behavior (typing + Enter), there are no custom key bindings - no arrow-key movement, no hotkeys. Native form submission is the only keyboard path.

claims.claim_text: A 'backToGames' Link to /student/games is rendered above the Header in all page states (loading, error, main) (page.tsx lines 512-517).
claims.interpretation: Navigation escape hatch is always present.

claims.claim_text: Restart is triggered from the GameEndScreen's onRestart callback wired to handleRestart (page.tsx lines 532-542); the RA copy wires BattleResults' restart Button (BattleResults.tsx lines 58-60).
claims.interpretation: The terminal surfaces provide the only restart control.

claims.claim_text: The rankings tab fetches '/api/v1/games/rpg-battle/ranking' only when activeTab === 'rankings' (StartScreen.tsx lines 40-59).
claims.interpretation: Rankings load lazily on tab activation; in advantage-games this endpoint does not exist (see RPG-ID-011), so the tab shows the empty/error state there.

claims.claim_text: No audio asset files exist for RPG Battle in the accepted asset denominator (zero audio-format candidates); all battle sounds are synthesized at runtime by useSound via WebAudio oscillators ('success' sine 880Hz, 'error' square 220Hz, 'missile-hit' sawtooth 110Hz).
claims.interpretation: RPG Battle audio is procedural; there is nothing to audit as an audio file asset.

claims.claim_text: The archived asset-spec (measure/archive/rpg_battle_20260102/asset-spec.md) defines the 3x3 pose grid mapping: (1,1) idle, (1,2) casting, (1,3) basic attack, (2,1) power attack, (2,2) hurt, (2,3) miss, (3,1) defend, (3,2) victory, (3,3) defeat; sheets face left and the player must be horizontally flipped.
claims.interpretation: The Sprite poseMap (RPG-ASSET-040) implements exactly this grid; the spec also explains Sprite's flip prop.

claims.claim_text: Sprite.tsx poseMap maps each of the 9 poses to {row,col} grid coordinates and renders via CSS background-position over a 3x3-scaled background (GRID_SIZE=3, backgroundSize 300% x 300%), with imageRendering 'pixelated' and optional scaleX(-1) flip.
claims.interpretation: Pose sheets are consumed as CSS sprites, not slicing; the player Sprite is rendered with flip=true (page.tsx line 577) to face the enemy.

claims.claim_text: Legacy components PlayerSprite.tsx and EnemySprite.tsx reference '/games/rpg-battle/hero_male_pose_sheet_3x3.png' and '/games/rpg-battle/enemy_slime_pose_sheet_3x3.png' via next/image with unoptimized; these non-vocabulary asset paths exist only under apps/advantage-games/public/games/rpg-battle/, not under reading-advantage/public.
claims.interpretation: PlayerSprite/EnemySprite are unreferenced by any page or other component (grep for importers finds only their own test files) and use pre-vocabulary-namespace paths; in reading-advantage those paths have no corresponding public file - dead code with a broken asset reference in the RA host.
claims.verification_command: grep -rn 'PlayerSprite|EnemySprite' apps/advantage-games/src apps/reading-advantage --include='*.tsx' --include='*.ts' (only self/test references); ls apps/reading-advantage/public/games/rpg-battle/ (missing)

claims.claim_text: Every sprite and background path referenced by rpgBattleSelection.ts and rpgBattleSprites.ts uses the '/games/vocabulary/rpg-battle/' prefix via withBasePath (10 distinct files: 2 hero sheets, 4 enemy sheets, 4 backgrounds).
claims.interpretation: All runtime-referenced assets resolve under public/games/vocabulary/rpg-battle/ and match denominator files one-to-one.

claims.claim_text: The reading-advantage page.tsx differs from the advantage-games page.tsx: it imports and renders BattleResults (line 33 import; lines 520-525 usage) instead of GameEndScreen, omits useGameFullscreen/useSession/useCurrentLocale, fetches vocabulary without a locale query param (line 147), and fetches unconditionally rather than gating on authentication.
claims.interpretation: The RA host copy is an older/leaner variant: no fullscreen, no auth gate on vocabulary fetch, no leaderboard-linked end screen.

claims.claim_text: In the reading-advantage page the terminal surface is BattleResults with props outcome=status, xp=resultXp, accuracy=resultAccuracy, onRestart=handleRestart (RA page.tsx lines 519-526).
claims.interpretation: RA shows the game-local BattleResults panel; advantage-games shows the shared GameEndScreen with leaderboard link.

claims.claim_text: The reading-advantage vocabulary fetch is fetch('/api/v1/games/rpg-battle/vocabulary') with no locale parameter (RA page.tsx line 147), whereas advantage-games appends ?locale=<currentLocale> (AG page.tsx lines 154-156).
claims.interpretation: Locale-aware vocabulary fetching exists only in the advantage-games copy.

claims.claim_text: Cross-host identical-content files (same SHA-256 in both hosts) include: useRPGBattleStore.ts, ActionMenu.tsx, BattleEffects.tsx, BattleLog.tsx, BattleResults.tsx, BattleScene.tsx, BattleSelectionModal.tsx, ComboIndicator.tsx, FloatingText.tsx, HealthBar.tsx, Sprite.tsx, PlayerSprite.tsx, EnemySprite.tsx and their test files (per T2 identical-hash-group reconciliation records).
claims.interpretation: Most of the RPG Battle implementation is byte-identical across hosts; the divergent files are page.tsx and StartScreen.tsx.

claims.claim_text: The reading-advantage StartScreen.tsx differs from the advantage-games copy: it adds unused Skull/Flame lucide imports (lines 7-8) and systematically downgrades text sizes (text-sm -> text-xs / text-[10px]) across 14 class strings; its full-file hash 8e4e9789... differs from the AG copy 9ed10cde....
claims.interpretation: StartScreen is the only component with a substantive cross-host divergence (smaller typography in RA); the Skull/Flame imports are unused elsewhere in the file (grep-verified).

claims.claim_text: The compliance-audit track apps/advantage-games/measure/tracks/rpg-battle-compliance-audit_20260426 (index.md, metadata.json, plan.md, report.md, spec.md) is present at the baseline and enumerated by the T2 source denominator.
